title: A bad key inside a form field's `publicPicker` reports the CONTAINER branch's diagnostic — the author is told to fix `viewKind`/`config`, not the key they typed
body:
Found while implementing #7485 (retiring the public lookup route's `picker.sort` read). Filed, not fixed: it is a pre-existing union-diagnostic defect in `ViewMetadataSchema`, unrelated to that card's ruling, and fixing it as a rider would have widened a route-only change into the shared view-parse error path.

## What happens

Saving a view whose form field carries an **unknown `publicPicker` subkey** through the real write path (`saveMetaItem` → `ViewMetadataSchema`) is correctly REFUSED — but the reported message describes a different failure entirely. Measured on this branch (`claude/issue-7485-retire-sort-read`, worktree, `@objectstack/spec` built from source), saving a `viewKind: 'form'` item whose field declares `publicPicker: { ...valid four keys, sort: [{ field: 'email', order: 'desc' }] }`:

```
[invalid_metadata] view/lead.contact failed spec validation: <root>: Invalid input;
<root>: Unrecognized key(s) on this view container: `viewKind`, `config`.
  • `viewKind` belongs to a single VIEW, not to the container. Wrap it:
    `defineView({ list: { type, data, columns, … } })`, or name it —
    `defineView({ listViews: { my_view: { … } } })`. The container's own keys are
    `list`, `form`, `listViews`, `formViews`. …
```

The word `sort` — the only thing actually wrong with the input — appears nowhere. The author is instead handed a confident, detailed, and **wrong** instruction: to restructure a container shape that was correct all along.

## Why

`ViewMetadataSchema` is a union. The ViewItem branch is the right branch and the one that fails (on `unrecognized_keys` for the picker subkey); the container branch also fails, on `viewKind`/`config` being unknown container keys. The surfaced error is the container branch's, so the diagnostic quality inverts: the branch that got FURTHEST is the one whose message is discarded.

The byte-identical item minus the bad subkey saves successfully, so the union does pick the ViewItem branch when it passes — this is purely about which failure is reported.

## Scope — it is not about `publicPicker`

`publicPicker` is just where it was noticed. Any ViewItem-branch parse failure on a `viewKind`-carrying item should reproduce it; the misleading `viewKind`/`config` text comes from the container branch and is independent of what the real error was. Worth confirming the general case before sizing a fix.

Note the direct door is fine: `FormViewSchema.safeParse` reports `unrecognized_keys` naming the key correctly (pinned in `packages/spec/src/ui/view-public-picker.test.ts`, `offset` case, since #7467). Only the union door degrades — which is the door `saveMetaItem` and therefore Studio uses.

## Why it matters

The measured cost is not "a vague error". It is an error that **names the wrong keys and prescribes a wrong fix with high confidence** — the failure mode Prime Directive #12 is about, and one an AI metadata author will follow straight into mangling a correct container.

## Sizing note

Not obviously a one-liner: it needs the union to pick a "best" failing branch (most-specific / deepest-progress) rather than reporting a fixed one, and any change there moves error text for every view-parse failure in the repo — including whatever baselines and pin tests currently encode today's messages. Worth its own card and its own reverse verification.

Related: #7485, #7467, #4001 (the container-shape messages this surfaces), ADR-0089 D3a.
